title: Patients Rated CBCT More Useful Than Periapicals Despite Limited Radiation Knowledge
html:
Most patients referred for endodontic assessment rated cone-beam computed tomography more useful than periapical radiography and reported greater confidence in their treatment plans after CBCT, even though most said they understood little about radiation. The findings come from a cross-sectional study published Nov. 13 in The Journal of the American Dental Association.

The study included 117 patients referred for endodontic assessment who underwent clinical assessment with both periapical radiography and CBCT. A two-part questionnaire measured radiation knowledge after the periapical images and changes in perception, confidence, and treatment acceptance after CBCT.

Baseline radiation knowledge was limited, with 59% rating their understanding as poor or very poor. Patients nonetheless prioritized diagnostic accuracy over a low radiation dose.

After CBCT, 79.5% of participants considered it more useful and helpful than periapical radiography, 60.7% reported increased confidence in their treatment plans, and 59.0% reported greater trust in their clinicians. And 89.7% said they would undergo CBCT for future care if clinically indicated.

The authors concluded that patients perceived the diagnostic benefits of CBCT as outweighing its risks. They recommended that clinicians explain both CBCT’s diagnostic advantages and its radiation risks, and strengthen the personalized consent process to address gaps in patients’ knowledge of ionizing radiation.

The study was conducted by Jonny Jin Myung Lee and Shanon Patel of the Faculty of Dentistry, Oral & Craniofacial Sciences at King’s College London, and Nassr Al-Nuaimi of Boston University’s Henry M. Goldman School of Dental Medicine, now with Tufts University School of Dental Medicine. The authors reported no disclosures.

The findings reflect patient perceptions in a referred endodontic population and do not address whether CBCT changed diagnoses or treatment outcomes.

Sources:
The Journal of the American Dental Association, “Cone-beam computed tomography in endodontics: patient perceptions, outcomes, and radiation awareness: A cross-sectional study,” published online Nov. 13, 2026: doi.org/10.1016/j.adaj.2026.07.029
